evals.prompt: This is the intro of our EJOR submission on battery scheduling (evals/files/ejor_intro.md). It reads like ChatGPT wrote it and my co-author hates it. Fix the wording for EJOR. Keep every citation and every number as it is, don't add anything new. Save the result as ejor_intro_revised.md.
evals.expected_output: A revised introduction in OR/EJOR register: no 'not X but Y', no dashes, related work reported neutrally (what SPO+ and Mandi et al. do and under which assumptions), no overclaiming ('dramatically', 'significantly' without test, 'novel', 'paradigm shift' removed or replaced by the numbers), all citations and numbers kept, no new claims; lint 0 errors.
assertions: Lint (check_wording.py, genre paper) reports 0 errors
No em-dashes or spaced dashes
No 'not X but Y' family
Related work is reported without grades (seminal, merely, fails to, suffers from, overlooks)
No intensifiers or hype (dramatically, significantly, novel, comprehensive, paradigm shift, pave the way)
'State of the art' removed, or kept with a question to the author in notes.md (a revision drops no claim)
Both cited works kept with their years (Elmachtoub and Grigas 2022; Mandi et al. 2020)
All numbers kept (31%, 24 months, 2021 to 2023, 12 MW, 24 MWh, 4.2 times)
No numbers that are not in the source

evals.prompt: Rewrite this section of my explainer in Simplified Technical English (evals/files/section-ste.html). Leave the chips, the equation and the figure id alone. Save it as section-ste_revised.html.
evals.expected_output: The same section in STE: sentences at most 25 words (Try instructions at most 20, imperative, one instruction per sentence), no semicolons, active voice, no phrasal verbs (carried out, set up, turns out, look at), same facts and numbers (94 %, 0.8 %, tau = 10), chips, equation div, figure id and math unchanged; lint --ste 0 errors.
assertions: Lint in STE mode (check_wording.py --ste, genre explainer) reports 0 errors
Source chips kept unchanged
Equation placeholder, figure id, derivation id and formula kept unchanged
Numbers kept (94 %, 0.8 %, tau = 10, slider 1 to 100)
No semicolons in the prose
No phrasal verbs of the source (carried out, set up, turns out, look at)
Try caption: imperative sentences of at most 20 words
Every sentence has at most 25 words

evals.expected_output: An abstract of 120 to 150 words in IS register: problem, theory (dual-process, fluency), the construct scrutiny cues introduced once, the experiment (N = 184, simple vs detailed) with the 64 % vs 41 % result, the contribution to theory and the design implication; 'significant' only tied to the test or replaced by the numbers; no numbers that are not in the notes; no 'not X but Y'; lint 0 errors.
assertions: Abstract has at most 150 words (the call's limit)
Abstract uses the space: at least 120 words
Lint (check_wording.py, genre abstract) reports 0 errors
Reports the sample and the main result (N = 184; 64% vs 41%)
No numbers that are not in the notes
'Significant' appears only together with its test, or not at all

States a contribution to theory (explains, theory)
No 'not X but Y' family and no em-dashes
